title: 2026 Season Power Rankings
subtitle: Pre-Week 7 board, post-waivers. Pocket stays No. 1 with its third kitty, the Eddies climb to No. 3 on four straight, and Saltese sent the OMVP leader to winless Drummond for Bijan. LAB flipped Demario Davis to Substation, TTAB is off the bus, and the BUF/JAX/LAC/WAS byes sideline Allen, Lawrence, Herbert and Daniels.
method: W/L + win quality + roster ceiling + FAAB + pedigree + sit/start + trades; PF is evidence, not the ranking.

rankings.blurb: Juice: the kitty is basically a lease at this point. Pocket's third of the year came at 262.5, five straight wins, and a 1706.0 PF that sits 167.5 clear of the field. Amani Hooker (36) and Tyler Shough (32) did the damage, and Shough takes the Saints to Paris on Sunday to face the Steelers. $98 is still the fattest wallet in the WU after a $3 Chig Okonkwo stash. Junk: the last two wins came by 7 and 3.5, which is not dominance, it's a magic trick. Will Anderson Jr. posted a 2 and gave away the DMVP lead, and Saquon is still parked in an IR slot. Hyper is next with the third-best PF and a quality-loss museum. Don't let them cut the ribbon on a new wing in your building.

Juice: four straight, 5-1, and the lowest PA in the league (1255.5), which is either great scheduling or a curse loading. Daniels (31) and Likely (28.5) led a 235.5 over the SPD's without needing a Warren encore. Then the front office got weird: Demario Davis, who was basically the whole defense in Week 4, went to Substation for Jihaad Campbell and rookie WR Carnell Tate. Daniels and the Commanders are on bye, so it's C.J. Stroud's week, and owning two starting QBs is exactly for weeks like this. Junk: Mike Evans, Jeremiyah Love and Caleb Douglas are all questionable in IR slots, and the PF is only fourth. 0-6 Drummond comes to town. Lose this one and the WU will bring it up at the draft.

Juice: four straight after an 0-2 start, and the Eddies have stopped asking for the quality-loss discount. Trevor Lawrence's 40 and George Karlaftis' 35 handled Substation 259.5–227.5, the defense put up 152, and the 1538.5 PF trails only Pocket. Lawrence and the Jaguars are on bye, so Bryce Young, the return from the Rhamondre swap, earns his keep this week. Junk: Breece Hall (quad) and Tyler Warren (groin) are both questionable, Garrett Wilson managed 8, and the backfield behind Hall is an IR ward (Etienne, Croskey-Merritt). Next up is a trip to Morningside, and Warren's Colts visit Justin Jefferson's 5-0 Vikings. Somebody's Sunday gets complicated.

Juice: 5-1, the second-lowest PA in the league, and a 189.5 that somehow kept them on the bus. Kittle (20.5), DK (20) and Quincy Williams (21) did just enough to beat TTAB by a field goal. Junk: Mahomes 8, Henry 5, Bucky 8, and T.J. Watt now has three points in two weeks. The 1430.5 PF is eighth, so this is a .500 résumé wearing a 5-1 jersey. Mahomes takes the unbeaten Chiefs into Seattle on Sunday night, and Saltese visits with a brand-new Bijan and a 259 that still lost. Pedigree doesn't tackle. Watt might want to try it.

Juice: two straight and the best defense of Week 6 at 160. Jeffery Simmons (38) and Budda Baker (31) turned Morningside into a walk, Drake Maye opens Week 7 on Thursday night in Chicago, and Gibbs gets the Packers at home. The team that rode the bus off in Week 1 now looks like the most dangerous 3-3 in the WU. Junk: the 1564.5 PA is second-worst, the wallet is at $0 after a $1 Demario Douglas grab, and James Cook is on the Bills' bye, so Dameon Pierce gets the call. Judkins and Pacheco are in IR slots, and Harold Fannin scored 1.5 on the winning side. Substation and its new Demario Davis host next.

Juice: the roster is better than 3-3. Jonathan Taylor, Zay Flowers, Tee Higgins and a healthy-again A.J. Brown, and Matthew Golden (30) was the only receiver who showed up at LAB. The SPD's spent on Jordan Battle, Jeremiah Trotter and Michael Mayer and cut Jalen Hurts on the way out the door. Junk: two straight losses, Brown and Adams combined for 11, Juwan Johnson laid a 0, and the trade block is basically the WR room. Adams is on IR, and Jordan Love, Golden and three linebackers all carry injury tags into Packers-Lions. A trip to Ultron is the kind of game a 3-3 team has to win.

Juice: Nabers (36), Ja'Marr Chase and George Pickens can win any week, and the offense actually beat the Eddies 130.5–107.5. Then the front office answered the obvious question and got Demario Davis from LAB for Jihaad Campbell and Carnell Tate. Still on the bus, too, which is more than half the league can say. Junk: the 97-point defense is why the two-game heater died, the wallet is down to $10, and RJ Harvey and Emmett Johnson are still the backfield. Alec Pierce came in and went straight to an IR slot. The Slumlords and their 160 defense are next, so Davis better unpack fast.

Juice: lost by 3, the third-lowest PA in the league, and went shopping like it was the trade deadline: Stefon Diggs from Saltese for $20 and Omar Cooper Jr. for $19. Junk: lost the game and the bus seat on one 3-point scoreboard, Cameron Skattebo put a 0 in a starting slot, and the wallet is at $0. Josh Allen's Bills and Diggs' Commanders are both on bye, so it's Bo Nix's week and the new WR debut waits. Last Ride is against Saltese, the team that sold them Diggs. Doubtpfizer comes to town. The Week 1 kitty is starting to look like the highlight of the season.

Juice: the third-best PF in the league (1519.5) and a 237 that beat eight other Week 6 scores. Walker (35), Jaylin Noel (32) and Travis Hunter (28) are real, and Walker gets a Sunday-night homecoming in Seattle with the unbeaten Chiefs. Junk: 2-4, and the quality-loss museum just added a new wing. Herbert posted a 7 and the 0-6 Chargers are on bye, so Kirk Cousins gets the start. Hunter's Jaguars are off too, and Egbuka sits in an IR slot. $25 went on Cousins, Michael Penix Jr. and Jalen Pitre. A trip to Pocket is the worst possible draw, and the record has stopped listening to the PF.

Juice: the dual-era champ finally got the whole roster to show up on one Sunday. CMC (31), Hubbard (29), and Singleton and Styles (29 each) beat Hyper 255–237, and Nakobe Dean now leads the DMVP race at 163. Fifth in PF, and $85 is the second-fattest wallet in the WU. Junk: a 1655.5 PA, worst in the league by 83, so the schedule is the real opponent. Rashee Rice and Mason Graham are questionable in IR slots, and Styles' Commanders are on bye. Dak gets the Eagles on Monday night. A trip to TTAB is a shot at back-to-back Ws and a pulse.

Juice: the blockbuster of the week. The OMVP leader (JSN, 197 YTD) and Jevon Holland went to winless Drummond for Bijan Robinson and Kyle Hamilton, less than a day after Diggs went to TTAB for $20. Bijan, Omarion Hampton and Aaron Jones is a loaded backfield, and Saltese still won't die on Last Ride after 259 buried Ultron. Junk: four straight losses, including the best losing score of Week 6. Hampton's Chargers are on bye, Parsons is still on PUP, and the WR room is DeVonta Smith (on the trade block) and Tre Tucker. Bijan's Falcons host the 6-0 Niners, Saltese visits the 5-1 Goats, and Last Ride is TTAB. Nobody in the WU has a weirder week.

Juice: 3-3 is a better record than five teams have, and the two guys on the trade block, Bobby Okereke (41) and Pete Werner (35), outscored the entire offense. Junk: that offense put up 70.5, the 1256.5 PF is dead last, and it's two straight losses. Jefferson and Kelce are both tagged in active slots, Lamar (Q) sits in reserve, and Deebo is out indefinitely. Aaron Rodgers gets the Steelers' Paris trip against Pocket's Shough. The 4-2 Eddies are coming to town, and the standings have been covering for this team for weeks.

Juice: got the W, 205.5–163 over Drummond, with Schwesinger (28) and the Swift/Tuten backfield (24 each) doing the work. Junk: the same 205.5 got buried by Saltese's 259 on Last Ride, so the re-entry dream is over. The 1259.0 PF is 13th, Myles Garrett, Terrance Ferguson and Kyle Monangai are all in IR slots, Terry McLaurin got dropped after a 3, and $2 is what's left. Tuten and Oluokun have the Jaguars' bye. Caleb Williams opens the week on Thursday night against Drake Maye. The SPD's come to town, and the Rhamondre swap had better start paying.

Juice: the OMVP leader just moved in. JSN (197 YTD) and Jevon Holland came over from Saltese, so JSN, Olave and Burrow is a passing game that should score in any league, Burrow's Bengals at Baltimore included. Junk: 0-6, six straight losses, and the week's floor at 163 on a 63-point offense. The trade sent out Bijan and Kyle Hamilton, whose 27 led the team in Week 6. Hockenson (concussion) and Turpin (ribs) are questionable, McConkey and D.J. Moore are in IR slots, and $1 is left. A trip to 5-1 LAB is next. Win one. Any one.
